title: Photon-starved imaging through turbulence at the diffraction limit
abstract: Atmospheric turbulence limits the resolution of ground-based imaging through rapidly evolving wavefront distortions. Fast acquisition can effectively freeze turbulence, but the restricted photon budget makes joint scene and wavefront recovery challenging. Here, we introduce Turbulence-Aware Poisson Blind Deconvolution (TAP-BD), which uses optical phase diversity to provide complementary measurements within a short acquisition window and increase wavefront information per detected photon. Poisson denoising and physics-informed optimization translate this information gain into joint recovery of the scene and a shared turbulence wavefront, with phase estimation errors approaching the Cramer--Rao lower bound in simulations. Experiments demonstrate reliable recovery from only a few tens of measurements under strong turbulence, with additional validation under severe photon scarcity. Simulations further show robustness to scintillation and temporal evolution over short acquisition windows. These results support photon-efficient imaging through turbulence, with potential applications in astronomy, remote sensing, and space situational awareness, particularly for time-sensitive observations.
